system_overview: This specification is a PlusCal representation of the Dijkstra-Scholten algorithm for detecting termination of a distributed computation initiated by a designated root node. Published by E.W. Dijkstra and C.S. Scholten in 'Termination detection for diffusing computations' (Information Processing Letters, 11(1):1-4, 1980). The algorithm maintains a spanning tree that contains all active nodes. Inactive leaf nodes detach themselves from the tree, but may later be reactivated by receiving a message and reattach. When the root node has no more children and becomes inactive, it declares termination.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a finite set of nodes, one of which is designated as the initiator (root). Each node operates as an independent process that can send base messages to other nodes, receive messages, terminate (become inactive), receive acknowledgments, and detach from the spanning tree or declare termination. A shared network provides message-passing infrastructure with per-sender message queues and acknowledgment counters for each node.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) a global termination detection flag indicating whether termination has been declared, (2) a network structure that for each node maintains a count of pending base messages from each sending node and a count of pending acknowledgment messages, (3) per-node activity status (active or inactive), (4) per-node parent pointer indicating the node's parent in the spanning tree or a sentinel value if the node has no parent, and (5) per-node count of active children (sons) in the spanning tree.
initial_state: Termination has not been detected. The network has no pending messages or acknowledgments. Only the initiator is active; all other nodes are inactive. The initiator's parent is itself; all other nodes have no parent. All nodes start with zero active children.
actions: Each node process runs in an infinite loop choosing nondeterministically among five operations: (1) Send message: an active node sends a base message to some other node, incrementing its active children count. (2) Terminate: an active node becomes inactive. (3) Receive message: a node receives a pending base message from some sender, becoming active. If the node has no parent, the sender becomes its parent; otherwise, an acknowledgment is sent back to the sender. (4) Receive acknowledgment: a node receives a pending acknowledgment, decrementing its active children count. (5) Detach or declare termination: when a node is inactive, has no active children, and has a parent, it either declares termination (if it is the initiator/root) or sends an acknowledgment to its parent and clears its parent pointer.
safety_properties: Termination detection is sound: the termination detected flag can only become true when the system is actually quiescent, meaning all nodes are inactive, no acknowledgments are pending, and no base messages are in transit between any pair of nodes.
liveness_properties: If the system reaches a quiescent state (all nodes inactive and no messages in transit), then termination is eventually detected.
model_bounds: The set of nodes and the maximum number of pending messages are declared as constants. A state constraint bounds the number of pending acknowledgments per node and the number of pending messages between any pair of nodes to keep the state space finite for model checking.
additional_assumptions: The set of nodes is finite. The initiator is a member of the node set. Weak fairness is assumed for each node process. The PlusCal algorithm is translated to TLA+ and the specification includes both the algorithmic description and the generated TLA+ translation.
